title: The popular version. The Library of Alexandria did not end in one fire.
description:
The Library of Alexandria did not end in one fire. Julius Caesar's civil war fire in 48 BC burned all or part of the collection, but it is unclear how much. Strabo mentions visiting the Mouseion around 20 BC.

It dwindled under the Romans. The Library declined through a lack of funding and support. Its membership appears to have ceased by the 260s AD.

Scholars had been driven out long before. In 145 BC Ptolemy VIII purged intellectuals from Alexandria. Aristarchus exiled himself to Cyprus and other scholars fled to other cities.

Nobody knows how many scrolls it held. Estimates range from 40,000 to 700,000 at its height.

Whatever remained probably went in the 270s AD. A Palmyrene invasion and an imperial counterattack between 270 and 275 AD probably destroyed what was left, if it still existed.

A second library may have outlived it. A daughter library in the Serapeum may have survived the main Library. The Serapeum was demolished in 391 AD under a decree from Bishop Theophilus.

It faded for centuries before anything finished it.
